To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ESG rating has a statistically significant effect on the return rates and their volatility of companies listed on the public market in Poland.
the higher the ESG rating, the lower the return rate volatility and the lower forecasting errors in return rates of the shares issued by the companies.

1) the ESG rating is a good indicator of the quality of non-financial data disclosure, 2) there is a large gap in the quality of non- financial data disclosure, 3) the ESG disclosure is a good predictor of the future return rate on shares issued by companies, and 4) the ESG data disclosure contributes to a reduction of the risk of investing in the shares of public companies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of ESG rating on the return rates of shares of companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
verifying the hypothesis that greater ESG reporting transparency results in lower return rate volatility and lower forecasting errors in the return rates of shares issued by public companies.
the impact of the level of non-financial data reporting on the return rate volatility of companies listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ESG rating is an additional source of information for investors, and therefore a tool for reducing the risk of investment decisions.
ESG reporting contributes to the creation of a more transparent and predictable capital market, which is conducive to the development of a sustainable economy.
the ESG rating is a useful tool for investors, which is confirmed by the research results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a positive correlation between a company's ESG rating and return rates.
the ESG rating is a good tool for assessing the risk–return profile in the portfolio, which can be applied to the Polish stock market.
the higher the quality of non-financial data reporting (the higher the ESG rating) the more stable and less risky are the return rates of shares issued by such companies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the level of ESG disclosure by companies listed on the Polish stock market is low and the level of EGS reporting is insufficient to allow for the creation of ESG indices and the implementation of the ESG factor in risk analysis of companies' investment portfolios.
the level of non-financial data reporting has a positive effect on the return rate volatility of the analysed companies.
ESG reporting is an effective tool to increase transparency of the public companies' operations, and hence to reduce information asymmetry on capital markets.
